summary_for_children: Surah Saba tells of Dawud, for whom iron was made soft, and Sulayman, for whom a spring of copper flowed. Then it tells of the people of Saba who had two beautiful gardens but turned away, and lost them in a flood.
world_title: Gardens of Saba and the Copper Spring
environment_concept: Hills that echo with praise and birds (34:10), a glowing spring of copper (34:12), great basins (34:13), gardens on both sides of a dam (34:15) and a broken one where the trees fell (34:16).
architecture_and_scenery: Mountains echoing praise, a forge, a flowing copper spring, great bowls like reservoirs, and the fertile valley of Saba behind a dam.

palette.lighting: Warm forge light and green valley sun
palette.atmosphere: Echoes in the mountains, water over the dam

unique_world.visual_theme: A stone dam between two hills holding rain water, with a garden of fruit trees on the left and on the right below it

primary_mechanic.text: Through a season of changing rain, open and close the sluice to each garden so both stay green, keep water in the dam, and patch cracks before they drain it. If a garden dries out, that month starts again. The two gardens are from 34:15; the flood (34:16) is read only, never played or shown.

secondary_activities: Dawud and the coats of mail (34:10-11, read only)
unique_world.narrative_structure: The sign, three months at the dam, then a reading
environment_behaviour: water runs down the open channels
garden ground and trees go from dry to green
water spills over the side when the dam is full
unique_world.learning_objective: Learn about the two gardens of Saba and the call to be grateful (34:15), by sharing water fairly

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Gardens and the Dam
story_library.children_narration: Allah gave Dawud and Sulayman remarkable blessings. The people of Saba also enjoyed beautiful gardens and abundant provision. But they were not grateful, and the Quran tells how a flood brought destruction to their gardens. The story reminds us that blessings should be appreciated and never taken for granted.

world_idea.title: The Gardens of Saba
world_idea.description: Explore two flourishing gardens and a large dam-inspired structure. Watch a narrated environmental transformation connected to the flood, and learn about water stewardship through a separate educational simulation.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The flood of the dam is narrated, not played as destruction. Dawud and Sulayman are not shown.
